questions.prompt: What happens when you press the clutch pedal?
options: The engine connects to the brakes
The engine disconnects from the gearbox
The car shifts up a gear by itself
questions.explanation: Pressing the pedal unclamps the clutch disc, so the engine can keep turning while the gearbox is free to change gear or stand still.

questions.prompt: Why does a car need a gearbox?
options: To keep the engine in its useful speed range at any road speed
questions.explanation: Low gears give lots of pulling force for setting off; high gears let the engine turn slowly at cruising speed.

questions.prompt: A clicking noise when turning sharply often points to…
questions.explanation: Outer CV joints work hardest at full steering lock. Once worn (often after the boot splits), they click in tight turns.

questions.prompt: In a front-wheel-drive car, what is the gearbox-plus-differential unit called?
questions.explanation: A transaxle puts the gearbox and differential in one case, which saves space in a front-wheel-drive car.
